steps.name: Anyone signs in with Google or an email link — there is no gate.
onCreate writes users/{uid} and turns any invites waiting for that address into inbox items.
Welcome: profile picture (Google's, or upload one), display name, time zone — then the invites, first.
No invites? 'Create your first board' — they are its admin.
A board admin types an email and picks a role: 'asha@x.com — editor'.
An invite is stored with a hash of a random token; it names the board, so she can read it before she can read the board.
The email goes out; if she already has an account, it is in her inbox too.
She signs up (or in) with that address and accepts — from the link or the inbox.
Her role, the board's readerUids and her members/ row commit together; Priya is told.
From now on she can be assigned, @mentioned and notified on that board, and on no other.
C, or Quick add under a column: 'Fix login redirect @priya !high due:fri'.
The card appears at once with a pending key ('ENG-…'); the request carries a clientId.
can(create), validation, required fields — then one transaction: key, ticket, activity.
The board's listener delivers the real document; the optimistic card is replaced by id.
Assignees and mentioned people are notified; a webhook fires; the search index updates.
A card is dragged from In progress to Review, between two others.
The browser computes a rank between its new neighbours and moves the card locally.
ticketUpdate: an editor may; a commenter only inside their StageGrant; 'requires' fields for Review must be set.
Refused → the card animates back and says why. Accepted → activity row and 'stage' notifications.
Everyone else with the board open sees it move, live.
Asha types in the composer, @-mentions Priya, links #ENG-40 and pastes a screenshot.
The screenshot uploads to Storage while she is still typing.
Send: the bubble appears immediately, marked sending.
The body is validated and its mentions and refs derived; message, counts and read pointer commit.
Priya gets 'mentioned' — in app, push, and email — regardless of her board mode.
Watchers get 'comment' through their board prefs; ENG-40's thread gets 'mentioned in ENG-42'.
Priya replies to the email; the reply lands in the same thread, via email.
An editor pins the decision; it floats to the top of the thread for everyone.
In ENG-40's description Asha writes 'needs #ENG-42 and #ENG-43 first'.
The refs are derived; ENG-42 and ENG-43 get ENG-40 in referencedBy and a 'referenced from ENG-40' line.
She also marks ENG-43 'blocks' ENG-40; ENG-40 gets 'blocked by ENG-43' in the same write.
Each drawer's Related panel shows both directions; ENG-40's card shows ⛔ blocked until ENG-43 is done.
The timeline draws the 'blocks' link as an arrow.

flows.name: Adding a custom field and a view over it

steps.name: An admin adds 'Client' (select: Acme, Globex) and 'Contract value' (currency INR).
boardUpdate appends two FieldDefs; no ticket is written.
The Field panel and the Table grow the two editors, because both render from board.fields.
Somebody groups the kanban by Client and filters 'Contract value > 5L', then Save as shared view.
Every 15 minutes, active tickets due within the next day are swept.
Each assignee's own lead time and channels decide who hears, where, and when.
A push: 'ENG-42 is due in 3 hours'.
Missed → 'overdue' on WhatsApp, for people who linked a number and asked for it.
dueNotified is stamped so the next sweep says nothing; moving the date re-arms it.
Account › Data & deletion; a fresh sign-in is required.
Refused if they are the only admin of a board other people are on; they hand it over or delete it.
Memberships end; the profile becomes 'Deleted user'; messages stay attributed to that.
The Auth user is deleted, which revokes every session and token.
You open Agents from the sidebar and make 'Builder': a picture, a one-line description and a Markdown system prompt.
agents/{ag_…} is written with you as its owner — nobody else can read it.
On ENG › People & roles you choose + Add agent, pick Builder and give it commenter with a stage grant of Build and Review.
boardAgentSet checks you are admin there and own Builder, then writes access, stageGrants and members/{agentId} with kind 'agent'. No invite is sent.
Builder now shows in the assignee picker and the @ menu, with its badge; Priya assigns it ENG-42.
notify() sees an agent among the recipients and writes an 'assigned' event to its inbox instead of a push.
Account › Tokens › New token: name orch-eng-builder, board ENG, acts as Builder, preset Worker, 90 days. The key is shown once with an MCP config and curl lines.
The hash, board, actsAs and scopes are stored under your account; archiving Builder or removing it from ENG would revoke it.

flows.name: Asking a question, and planning the work

steps.name: Ada is stuck on ENG-42 and needs Grace to choose. In the composer she presses ❓ (or types /ask), starts from 'Pick one', writes the question, types two options, names Grace and leaves Blocking on.

Ask posts through the outbox, so the card is in the thread before the server answers. questionAsk writes a message of kind 'question' with the form in `question`, rolls ticket.waitingOn up for the ❓ badge and notifies Grace.
Grace sees ❓ Waiting for you on the board card without opening the ticket, opens it, picks an option and writes a line in 'Anything else?'.

questionAnswer locks the question in place (one field on the message), posts Grace's answer as her own reply bubble, clears ticket.waitingOn and — if an agent had asked — files a question_answered event in its inbox.
With the answer in hand Ada plans the work: + New list in the right pane, a title, and five pasted lines that become five items.
tasklistSet writes boards/{b}/tickets/{t}/tasklists/{listId} with Ada as its owner, rolls ticket.tasklistProgress up for the card chip and says it once in the thread ('Ada added a plan: …').

As the work happens she clicks items through todo → doing → done, marks one skipped and one failed with a note. Builder, the agent on the ticket, ticks items off ITS own list beside hers — and Ada can tick those too.
tasklistItemUpdate changes the one item and the roll-up, and says nothing in the thread — ticking is not news. The card chip sums every list on the ticket, whoever owns it.
